transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hicks (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Priya Narang (Redwood SRE); Maya Chen (HelixCare Infra Lead); Carlos Rivera (HelixCare Platform Eng); Nina Boyd (HelixCare Security); Evan Lowe (HelixCare DevOps)

Summary: quick results review from week 7 of the Private/VPC pilot, focused on networking anomalies, routing fallback behaviour, kernel upgrade plan and next steps for validation. Some packet level weirdness remains (MTU-related fragmentation on one path).

Topics: network jitter and egress shaping, canary kernel upgrade, KV cache warmup, fallback routing policy, audit logs / KMS checks, perf regression triage.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everybody, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep to 45, got a few items on the readout from last week's runs. Maya you mentioned you had fresh logs — do you want to kick us off?
[00:12] Maya (HelixCare): yeah, thanks. um, quick note — we ran the smoke tests against the private canary cluster on tuesday and thursday. overall the latency looked stable but there was a set of tail spikes between 180 and 280ms when the egress path hit the firewall, so we think it's an MTU / fragmentation issue, and maybe a reassembly timeout in one of our middleboxes.
[00:33] Carlos (HelixCare): to add to that, when we triggered the fallback routing policy the KV cache warmup didn't persist across the fallback, so the first two requests saw cold KV hits and multi-token latency increased, that explains some of the P95 rise.
[00:50] Samir (Redwood): okay that's interesting — are those fallbacks going to our dedicated peering in region or are they re-routing to the public egress? we had planned the fallback to a same-region variant but the trace we saw looked like it went out-of-region for three minutes.
[01:07] Evan (HelixCare): yep, ended up hitting an out-of-region path for like two to three minutes; we think an intermediate router flapped and the route-map preference inverted. we've got the BGP session logs attached but haven't correlated with the full packet captures yet.
[01:22] Priya (Redwood): one quick note — the runtime we shipped last week has a kernel build with a defensive MTU fragment guard, it's lightweight, but we also added a flag that avoids dynamic reassembly in the fast path. Jordan — we pushed a patch to the canary image.
[01:35] Jordan (Redwood): right — and we want to hear from you if that changed the tail behaviour. Maya?
[01:40] Maya (HelixCare): we pulled the image on two canaries wednesday night. initial results looked better for the big tokens, but then on Thursday we saw a regression when the canary hit a combination of Nagle + small packet bursts, I'm not sure if the kernel flag created a head-of-line effect.
[01:57] Samir (Redwood): hmm, okay so possibly the fast-path de-queued different sizes — we might be seeing queuing at the NIC driver level. we should capture with tcpdump and look for retransmit patterns.
[02:10] Nina (HelixCare): also flagging security — our compliance team asked about audit logs for fallback events, they need a per-request reason code, e.g., "fallback:capacity" or "fallback:egress". is that something Redwood can emit?
[02:24] Samir (Redwood): yes, we can add a structured fallback reason in the trace. currently we emit a generic code, but adding a more granular tag is straightforward — we can include it in the request-level log and the per-route dashboard.
[02:36] Jordan (Redwood): quick pause — I want to confirm success criteria for the week: HelixCare wants P95 under 120ms for steady-state, and no more than 3 percent token loss during failover; also security needs the fallback reason in logs. is that fair?
[02:51] Maya (HelixCare): yes that's accurate. and we also want reproducible steps for the kernel rollback in case we need to revert mid-morning during business hours.
[02:59] Jordan (Redwood): got it. ok next, perf numbers — Samir?

[03:05] Samir (Redwood): so we ran the 10k request load across canaries; baseline (pre-patch) P50 28ms, P95 140ms, P99 420ms during the incident window. post-patch on canaries (with the MTU guard) P50 30ms, P95 122ms, P99 330ms. so P95 improved but P99 still shows sporadic long tails when fallback is triggered. that aligns with CX's KV cache warmup note.
[03:36] Carlos (HelixCare): when the fallback happened the cache-invalidation event was a byproduct of a route change; we had TTLs set low in one region so the cache entries expired and we saw misses. maybe TTL tuning would help.
[03:49] Priya (Redwood): TTL tuning can help but also we can snapshot KV state and pre-warm during canary promotion; Samir and I sketched a warmup handshake that exchanges cache digests before shifting traffic.
[04:04] Maya (HelixCare): that could work. curious though, you mentioned the warmup requires a handshake window — how long is that expected to take for our model sizes?
[04:12] Samir (Redwood): depends on the KV footprint; for your test set it's about 300ms to transfer digests and warm the top 5% hot keys if we stream asynchronously; full warmup of large contexts is more expensive, but incremental warmup will give you immediate wins.

[04:30] [Short crosstalk — "yeah" "uh-huh"]

[04:38] Jordan (Redwood): ok on the kernel upgrade plan — we propose a staged rollout: patch canary nodes (already done), run a 24-hour soak with smoke tests and packet captures, then promote to 20% production with KV warmup enabled, then 100% if stable. we also will maintain an automated rollback trigger if error rate > 1 percent or P95 jumps > 30 percent.
[04:59] Maya (HelixCare): that's reasonable. for the rollback we need the exact CLI steps and the timeframe to revert, ideally under 15 minutes.
[05:07] Priya (Redwood): yes we'll provide an idempotent rollback script and a runbook with command snippets.

[05:15] [00:05:15] Carlos (HelixCare): about the routing policy — we saw an unintended behaviour where the traffic split on canary promotion still used the regional egress for some flows; I suspect a route preference tie-break in the vendor's switch. we've opened a ticket with their support but it may take days.
[05:33] Samir (Redwood): as a mitigation we can push an explicit source-based route for the canary IP block to prefer the private peering. that's a short-term fix and reversible.
[05:44] Evan (HelixCare): that makes sense. we can try that during the maintenance window.

[05:52] Nina (HelixCare): security question — KMS: where are keys stored? we need to validate that Redwood-managed keys are not used for PII paths; HelixCare requires customer-managed KMS for any PHI tokens.
[06:04] Jordan (Redwood): yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS; in your current env you've configured the regional KMS with granular key policies, correct?
[06:13] Nina (HelixCare): yes but we want to see the integration test results. can Redwood share the KMS access audit for the last 7 days?
[06:20] Priya (Redwood): we can export an audit bundle. we'll redact internal metadata but provide the access events for the service principal tied to your project.

[06:30] [00:06:30] Jordan (Redwood): alright next item — telemetry gaps. Maya, you mentioned there were missing traces correlated to the early morning failover?
[06:38] Maya (HelixCare): correct — there were about 12 requests that had no corresponding trace and the logs had only partial HTTP headers; we think some log forwarder buffer overflowed when consoles spiked. Carlos - can you confirm which logshipper was running?
[06:50] Carlos (HelixCare): we used fluentd in daemonset mode; we saw ouput backpressure on node 3 where the log emitter blocked for 4s. we'll drop the buffer and re-run.
[06:58] Samir (Redwood): okay good catch — that's consistent with the tail spikes; missing traces make it hard to map exact token-level behavior during failover. run the same job with larger fluentd buffers and we can correlate again.

[07:08] Jordan (Redwood): action wise, Redwood will ship a quick validation script that exercises fallback, collects pcap, and captures application traces and fluentd logs. that'll make replication straightforward.
[07:20] Maya (HelixCare): sounds good. one ask from ops: can Redwood include an example of how to trigger the KV warmup pre-promotion? a scripted curl + warmup header would be super helpful.
[07:29] Samir (Redwood): yes we have that. we'll attach a snippet and a small go/python tool in the repo.

[07:36] [00:07:36] Carlos (HelixCare): another note — cost. during the canary the GPU utilization dipped because of warmup overhead, so unit costs spiked ~12% for that window. is there a recommended approach to amortize warmup costs?
[07:50] Priya (Redwood): the typical approach is to pre-warm during low-cost windows or use a burst capacity reservation for the brief warmup window. Redwood Optimize also has a suggestion engine that will size warmup batches to minimize overhead. we can share a cost analysis.
[08:07] Maya (HelixCare): okay we'd like to see that cost/benefit before rolling to 20%.

[08:12] Jordan (Redwood): sure — we'll produce a one-page cost delta with warmup vs no-warmup. Samir will own that.

[08:20] [00:08:20] Nina (HelixCare): compliance — any new telemetry retention implications from adding fallback reason codes? we need to ensure logs with PII tokens are not retained longer than 30 days.
[08:31] Priya (Redwood): fallback reason codes are small strings we attach to traces; we do not change token retention policies. we'll provide a certification note that log tagging won't alter retention window.

[08:40] Jordan (Redwood): great. to recap key decisions: 1) push the kernel patch on canaries (done) and run 24h soak; 2) Redwood to provide rollback script and runbook; 3) implement KV warmup handshake and sample scripts; 4) HelixCare to run smoke tests and packet captures; 5) Redwood to add structured fallback reason to logs; 6) run cost/benefit for warmup before 20% promotion.

[08:58] Maya (HelixCare): and one more — can we have an emergency rollback contact list with phone numbers in the runbook? business continuity wants a primary/secondary cc.
[09:07] Jordan (Redwood): yes we'll add on-call contacts and escalation matrix to the runbook.

[09:15] [00:09:15] Samir (Redwood): quick note on diagnostics — when you upload pcaps name them with the canary id and timestamp; we'll correlate with request-ids — sometimes request-ids are missing due to header trimming so please include the full http headers.

[09:28] Carlos (HelixCare): ok will do.

[09:32] Jordan (Redwood): any blockers for next week?
[09:35] Maya (HelixCare): the only blocker is the vendor switch ticket — if that extends beyond 48 hours we may not be able to force the explicit route quickly. but otherwise we can do the mitigation.
[09:45] Jordan (Redwood): understood. we'll treat that as a risk.

[09:50] [00:09:50] Closing: Jordan: thanks everyone — action items in the ticket. we'll email the patch and runbook within 48 hours. next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc post-patch check.
[09:59] Maya: thanks all.
[10:02] End of call.
